key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings require a parameter trade-off: the lowest friction conditions did not deliver the highest wear resistance.
engineering_relevance: Tuning spraying conditions can improve coatings for restoring and surface-strengthening machine components.
method: Varied barrel filling from 48–68%, working-gas O/C ratio from 1.026–1.856, and inter-shot delay from 0–1 s.
Examined coating morphology, thickness, porosity, and microcracks.
Measured friction, specific wear rate, roughness, and hardness.
evidence_signal: Reported results included minimum friction of 0.674 ± 0.136, best specific wear rate of 0.000189 mm³/(N·m), roughness reduction from 5.00 to 3.60 µm, and maximum hardness of 905.6 HV under differing conditions.
watch_item: Do not treat these best-case metrics as one operating point; the abstract does not establish a single parameter combination that optimizes all properties.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
